theory.intro: A **frequency histogram** has a column for each score, and a **frequency polygon** joins the tops of those columns. A **cumulative frequency histogram** and its **ogive** show the running total instead.
facts: In a **frequency histogram** the columns are equal width and touch each other, and the frequency axis starts at $0$.
A **frequency polygon** joins the midpoints of the column tops and drops to the horizontal axis at an empty class at each end.
In a **cumulative frequency histogram** the height of each column is the cumulative frequency $cf$.
The **ogive** joins the top-right corners of the cumulative columns, starting at height $0$ at the lower boundary of the first class.
The **mode** is the score under the tallest column of the frequency histogram.
To estimate the **median**, find $0.5 \times n$ on the cumulative axis, go across to the ogive, then read down.
Read $Q_1$ at $0.25 \times n$ and $Q_3$ at $0.75 \times n$, then $IQR = Q_3 - Q_1$.
steps: Identify whether the graph is a frequency display (bars show individual frequencies) or a cumulative frequency display (bars show running totals).
To find the mode, locate the score under the tallest column on the frequency histogram.
To estimate the median or percentiles from an ogive, calculate the target cumulative frequency (e.g. $0.5 \times n$ for the median, $0.25 \times n$ for $Q_1$, $0.75 \times n$ for $Q_3$).
Locate the target value on the vertical cumulative frequency axis, project horizontally to intersect the ogive, and read vertically down to the horizontal axis.

foundation.question_text: State the key difference between where points are plotted when drawing a frequency polygon versus when drawing an ogive.
foundation.solution_text:
A frequency polygon connects points plotted at the **class centres** of each column at height equal to frequency $f$.
An ogive connects points plotted at the **upper class boundaries** (top-right corners) at height equal to cumulative frequency $cf$, starting at the lower boundary of the first class at height $0$.

The tallest column corresponds to mark $6$ with a column height of $12$.
$\text{Modal mark} = 6\text{ with frequency } 12$

At score $70$, the cumulative frequency is $42$ (students scoring $70$ or less).
$\text{Students scoring more than } 70 = 60 - 42$
$= 18$

development.solution_text:
$n = 80$
$\text{Median position} = 0.5 \times 80 = 40$
At $cf = 40$ (height $2.5$), read across to the segment between $(20, 32)$ and $(30, 60)$:
$\text{Interpolated time} = 20 + \frac{40 - 32}{60 - 32} \times 10 = 20 + \frac{8}{28} \times 10 \approx 23\text{ minutes}$
$\text{Median} \approx 23\text{ minutes}$

$n = 80$
$Q_1\text{ at } cf = 0.25 \times 80 = 20 \implies Q_1 \approx 34$
$Q_3\text{ at } cf = 0.75 \times 80 = 60 \implies Q_3 \approx 67$
$IQR = Q_3 - Q_1$
$= 67 - 34$
$= 33$

development.question_text: Why is a frequency polygon extended to the horizontal axis at empty class centres on both sides?
development.solution_text: Extending the polygon to the horizontal axis at zero frequency closes the polygon shape and ensures the total area under the frequency polygon equals the total area of the frequency histogram.

$n = 40$
$\text{Median cumulative frequency} = 0.5 \times 40 = 20$
The cumulative frequency reaches $20$ in the column for score $17$ (where $cf$ rises from $12$ to $26$).
$\text{Median} = 17$

$80\text{th percentile corresponds to } cf = 0.80 \times 100 = 80$
At $cf = 80$ (height $4.0$), read across to the segment between $(60, 65)$ and $(80, 85)$:
$\text{Score} = 60 + \frac{80 - 65}{85 - 65} \times 20 = 60 + \frac{15}{20} \times 20 = 75$
$80\text{th percentile} = 75$

Cumulative frequency at $50$ marks is $44$.
Cumulative frequency at $30$ marks is $16$.
$\text{Students scoring between } 30 \text{ and } 50 = 44 - 16 = 28$
$\text{Percentage} = \frac{28}{50} \times 100\% = 56\%$

development.question_text:
A cumulative frequency histogram has consecutive column heights of $5, 14, 28, 38, 44$.
What is the individual frequency of the third class interval?
development.solution_text:
The frequency of a class is the difference between its cumulative frequency and the preceding cumulative frequency.
$f_3 = cf_3 - cf_2$
$= 28 - 14$
$= 14$

mastery.question_text:
An ogive of $120$ exam marks has $Q_1 = 42$ and $Q_3 = 74$.
Calculate the interquartile range ($IQR$), determine the upper outlier fence ($Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR$), and state whether a student who scored $95$ is an outlier.
mastery.solution_text:
$IQR = Q_3 - Q_1$
$= 74 - 42$
$= 32$
$\text{Upper fence} = Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR$
$= 74 + 1.5(32)$
$= 74 + 48$
$= 122$
$95 < 122$, so a score of $95$ is not an outlier.

mastery.question_text:
A frequency polygon has vertices at $(15, 4), (25, 10), (35, 16), (45, 8), (55, 2)$ where the $x$-coordinates are class centres and $y$-coordinates are frequencies.
Calculate the estimated mean $\overline{x}$.

Two cumulative frequency ogives for cohorts of $60$ students show that Cohort A has a median of $52$ with $IQR = 22$, while Cohort B has a median of $64$ with $IQR = 14$.
Compare the performance and consistency of the two cohorts.
mastery.solution_text:
Cohort B had a higher median ($64 > 52$), indicating a higher typical performance.
Cohort B had a smaller interquartile range ($14 < 22$), indicating more consistent scores than Cohort A.
Cohort B achieved higher typical scores with greater consistency.
